basis: 2 of 25 tracked indices rose in their latest session.

Rule: Risk-on = 65%+ of indices up and VIX not rising; Risk-off = 35% or fewer up, or VIX up 8%+; otherwise Mixed.

headline.technical: US stocks fell on AI jitters ahead of Nvidia's results (S&P 500 -1.92%), with FT and WSJ reporting global selling led by chip stocks and Asian and European indices lower on Tuesday.
headline.layman: Shares fell in many countries as investors worried about AI before Nvidia reports its results.

global.title: AI worries and chip curbs drive a global stock dip

status.technical: S&P 500 closed -1.92% and Nasdaq Composite -2.49%. The FT reported investors fretting over tighter US chip export controls and a possible slowdown in AI data centre build-out; Business Standard reported semiconductor shares led losses. VIX closed at 23.43.
status.layman: US stocks fell sharply on Monday and many other markets slipped Tuesday. The Financial Times says investors worry about new US limits on chip exports and about AI spending slowing down.

consequence.technical: If Nvidia's results and guidance show customers keep spending on AI data centres, the concern flagged by Euronews could ease; if not, pressure on chip stocks could persist. The notes do not say which is more likely.
consequence.layman: If Nvidia shows that its customers are still spending heavily on AI, worries could ease. If not, chip shares could stay under pressure. The notes do not say which way it will go.

impact.technical: Chipmakers are hit hardest. Straits Times reported data centre REITs and related stocks slid after the new US rule on AI chip exports, though analysts there said underlying demand should still help operators. Nvidia shares are set for a $335 billion swing after earnings, per Investing.com options data.
impact.layman: Chip companies are hit most. Companies that run data centres also fell, although analysts say demand for AI and cloud computing should still help them. Options pricing points to a very big move in Nvidia after its results.

outlook.technical: Base rates, not predictions: after S&P 500 falls larger than 1 standard deviation, the next day rose 48% of 153 times (median -0.05%) and the next 5 days rose 58% of 153 times (median 0.4%).
outlook.layman: This is history, not a forecast. After similar big falls in the S&P 500, the next day was higher 48% of the time and the next 5 days were higher 58% of the time.

regions.title: Americas: tech-led slide, Brazil under pressure

status.technical: Straits Times reported US stocks closing sharply lower on AI jitters ahead of Nvidia results and the Anthropic IPO. Nasdaq Composite -2.49%, S&P 500 -1.92%, Dow -1.41%. Bloomberg reported Lula worries hitting Brazil markets from the real to corporate bonds; Bovespa -1.83%.
status.layman: US shares dropped, with tech falling the most. In Brazil, Bloomberg says worries about President Lula hurt the currency, shares and company bonds.

consequence.technical: If the Nvidia print eases AI concerns, US tech could stabilise; the notes give no basis for a Brazil call beyond Bloomberg's report of political worry.
consequence.layman: If Nvidia's news calms AI fears, US tech could steady. The notes do not explain how Brazil's worries might play out.

impact.technical: US tech and chip names bear the brunt; in Brazil the Bloomberg report points to currency, equity and credit markets alike.
impact.layman: US tech investors are most affected. In Brazil, savers in shares, bonds and the currency all feel it.

outlook.technical: Base rates, not predictions: after Nasdaq Composite falls larger than 1 standard deviation, the next day rose 50% of 170 times (median 0.01%) and the next 5 days rose 55% of 170 times (median 0.35%).
outlook.layman: This is history, not a forecast. After similar big falls in the Nasdaq, the next day was higher 50% of the time and the next 5 days were higher 55% of the time.

regions.title: Europe: modest dip after record highs

status.technical: Euro Stoxx 50 closed -0.91%, DAX -0.78%, FTSE 100 -0.72%. Morningstar's early call saw the FTSE 100 lower after the US tech sell-off. Brussels raised Eurozone growth forecasts as the AI boom drives exports, with France's GDP projection halved, per the FT.
status.layman: European markets slipped less than US ones. Morningstar says the US tech sell-off dragged London lower. Meanwhile Brussels raised its growth forecasts for the euro area because AI is boosting exports.

consequence.technical: If AI-linked export strength persists as the European Commission expects, growth support could continue; Bloomberg notes inflation is proving more stubborn than policymakers expected.
consequence.layman: If AI keeps lifting exports, Europe's growth could stay solid. Bloomberg says inflation is stickier than officials expected.

impact.technical: The FT highlights diverging fortunes among the bloc's biggest economies, with France's forecast cut sharply.
impact.layman: Not every country gains equally. The FT says France's growth forecast was cut by a lot.

outlook.technical: Base rates, not predictions: after Euro Stoxx 50 falls larger than 1 standard deviation, the next day rose 53% of 159 times (median 0.14%) and the next 5 days rose 55% of 159 times (median 0.23%).
outlook.layman: This is history, not a forecast. After similar falls in European shares, the next day was higher 53% of the time and the next 5 days were higher 55% of the time.

regions.title: Asia-Pacific: chip selloff hits Korea and Taiwan

status.technical: KOSPI -2.59% and TAIEX -2.31%. Economic Times reported KOSPI closed at its lowest level since February on Nvidia caution. Business Standard reported chip shares led losses globally. Bloomberg cited Barclays attributing the Taiwan rout to forced retail liquidation. India bucked the trend: Nifty 50 0.38%.
status.layman: Korea and Taiwan fell the most because they are home to many chip companies. Barclays says forced selling by small investors hurt Taiwan. India's market rose a little.

consequence.technical: If forced retail liquidation fades, Taiwan selling pressure could ease, per the Barclays view reported by Bloomberg; Korean pressure is tied to Nvidia caution in the Economic Times report.
consequence.layman: If forced selling by small investors slows, Taiwan's drop could ease. Korea's drop is linked to nervousness about Nvidia.

impact.technical: Chipmakers and their foreign holders are most exposed; Economic Times reported foreign investors as net sellers in Korea.
impact.layman: Chip companies and foreign investors in Korea are most affected.

outlook.technical: Base rates, not predictions: after TAIEX falls larger than 1 standard deviation, the next day rose 60% of 152 times (median 0.18%) and the next 5 days rose 60% of 150 times (median 0.9%).
outlook.layman: This is history, not a forecast. After similar big falls in Taiwan's market, the next day was higher 60% of the time and the next 5 days were higher 60% of the time.

drivers.title: Nvidia earnings and US chip export curbs

status.technical: CNBC reported the US Commerce Department is moving to tighten export controls and Nvidia warned chip buyers of legal risks tied to China AI access. The FT reported Nvidia created a committee to oversee export-control compliance.
status.layman: The US is moving to tighten limits on chip exports. CNBC says Nvidia warned customers about legal risks around China. The FT says Nvidia set up a committee to oversee these rules.

consequence.technical: If controls tighten further, the China revenue ambitions criticised in Washington, per the FT, could be constrained; the notes do not quantify this.
consequence.layman: If limits get tighter, Nvidia's plans to sell more in China could be held back. The notes do not say by how much.

impact.technical: Chipmakers, data centre operators and US firms exposed to China, per CNBC's report on a growing China dilemma.
impact.layman: Chip companies, data centre firms and US companies that do business in China.

outlook.technical: Base rates, not predictions: after Nasdaq Composite falls larger than 1 standard deviation, the next 5 days rose 55% of 170 times (median 0.35%).
outlook.layman: This is history, not a forecast. After similar big Nasdaq falls, the next 5 days were higher 55% of the time.

status.technical: WSJ reported US stocks slipping on inflation and AI worries and gold pressured by Fed rate-hike bets. The US 10-year yield closed at 5.12; WSJ reported yields edged lower as investors awaited fresh drivers.
status.layman: WSJ says worries about prices and AI pushed US stocks down, and bets on higher US interest rates are weighing on gold. Government borrowing costs are high.

consequence.technical: If inflation keeps pushing yields up, Morningstar's note says it is not worried, while WSJ points to rate-hike bets; the notes show differing views.
consequence.layman: If prices keep rising, borrowing costs could stay high. Analysts quoted in the notes disagree on how worried to be.

impact.technical: Gold is pressured by rate-hike bets per WSJ; equity valuations face yield competition as implied by the notes' inflation worries.
impact.layman: Gold is under pressure. Savers earn more on bonds when yields are high.

outlook.technical: Base rates, not predictions: after S&P 500 falls larger than 1 standard deviation, the next 5 days rose 58% of 153 times.
outlook.layman: This is history, not a forecast. After similar S&P 500 falls, the next 5 days were higher 58% of the time.

events.title: Nvidia earnings, first since Jensen Huang's resignation
events.technical: Euronews said investors will scrutinise Nvidia's future outlook and whether customers keep spending heavily on AI data centres.
events.layman: Investors want to know if companies will keep spending big on AI.

events.title: Trump-Xi summit
events.technical: Bloomberg said economic security is high on the agenda ahead of Trump's summit with Xi.
events.layman: The US and China leaders meet later this week, and trade and security are on the agenda.

events.title: South Korea suspends aircraft ops; markets open late
events.technical: CNBC reported South Korean markets will open late because of a nationwide aircraft suspension during a college entrance exam.
events.layman: Korean markets open late on Thursday because of an exam-day flight pause.

companyEffects.technical: Investing.com reported options imply a $335 billion swing after earnings; Business Standard reported US chipmakers falling 5.3 per cent and FT cited fresh selling pressure on Nvidia.
companyEffects.layman: Nvidia is the centre of the AI worry. Options point to a very big move after its results, and chip shares fell hard.
